outcome: Give authorised care teams a source-linked view of relevant history across approved records; benefits are faster chart review, fewer missed facts, improved handoffs, and transparent provenance.
overview: Care teams lose time searching long, duplicated and fragmented records scattered across EHRs, exchanges and documents — and the facts they miss become handoff risks. This solution gives authorised clinicians a question-specific, source-linked view of relevant history: it aggregates approved records over HL7 FHIR, enforces identity and consent, and produces summaries in which every fact carries a citation and a date, with contradictions surfaced rather than smoothed over. Clinicians correct the summary, and corrections are audited; nothing writes back silently. An 8–12-week pilot targets a 30% reduction in selected chart-review time with completeness thresholds met and every access recorded.

benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate against timed chart-review baselines in the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Fewer missed facts at handoff through cited, date-stamped summaries that surface contradictions
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on source coverage and data quality; measured against fact/citation completeness thresholds agreed with clinicians, with clinician review always required

benefits.text: Full transparency — every access, citation and clinician correction is recorded
benefits.source: Reference architecture audit design, Redington Healthcare catalogue,
benefits.limits: A design property of the access and correction workflow, verified in UAT

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); patient records stay in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations and exchange rules

notFor.situation: No lawful basis or governance for cross-system record access
notFor.why: Aggregation without consent enforcement and lawful exchange is a privacy breach, not an interoperability solution

notFor.situation: No reliable patient-identity matching across the candidate sources
notFor.why: Wrong-patient merges are the highest-severity failure mode; identity matching is a hard precondition

notFor.situation: Expectation that summaries replace the legal medical record
notFor.why: Summaries are a cited navigation layer over the record; the source systems remain the system of record, per the source catalogue

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns identity policy, consent model and clinical safety review · Duration: 8–12-week pilot; 20–32 weeks to scaled deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, interoperability engineer, clinical-NLP engineer; customer CMIO or clinical lead, interoperability lead, information-governance owner, privacy and security approvers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Source and identity discovery with baseline agreement
2) Identity-matching validation and consent configuration
3) Source integration and normalisation
4) Clinical relevance, factuality and safety evaluation
5) Controlled pilot with weekly safety review
6) Stabilisation, benefit review and handover
